en: Jātaka:
The Collection of Threes, Chapter on Intention (Saṅkappavagga)
10. The Dūta Jātaka:
"To whom they come from afar, even to beg of an enemy,"
“I am the messenger of his inner self;
do not be angry with me, O bull among charioteers.
“[He] for whom [there is mindfulness] by day and by night...”
The young men fall under its power;
I am but a messenger from his belly,
so do not be angry with me, O bull among charioteers.
I give you, O brahmin,
a thousand red cows together with a bull;
for how could I not give to a messenger what belongs to a messenger?
"May we also become his messengers.
The Tenth Jātaka, the Messenger Jātaka.
The First Chapter, the Chapter on Intentions.
Its summary verse:
The excellent fletcher, a handful of sesame, a jewel,
the king of horses, a bird, and a venomous snake.
Janasandha [gave] a hundred thousand kahāpaṇas;
Tiriṭa, moreover, ten times that amount by way of the best of messengers.
